senses.definition: (literary) A whispering or rustling sound; a murmur.

quotes.text: [Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi was] pelted with buckets of water by firemen, and, finally, currycombed and rubbed down by two grooms, keeping a sharp susurrus between them, so as to soothe his wounded feelings; […]
quotes.reference: 1847 February, Thomas De Quincey, “Notes on Walter Savage Landor”, in Leaders in Literature with a Notice of Traditional Errors Affecting Them (De Quincey’s Works; IX), London: James Hogg & Sons, →OCLC, pages 312–313:

quotes.text: The soft susurrus and sighs of the branches.
quotes.reference: 1847 November 1, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, Evangeline, a Tale of Acadie, Boston, Mass.: William D. Ticknor & Company, →OCLC, (please specify either |part=I or II):

quotes.text: They heard the Green Fork before they saw it, an endless susurrus, like the growl of some great beast.
quotes.reference: 2000 August 8, George R[aymond] R[ichard] Martin, “”, in A Storm of Swords (A Song of Ice and Fire; 3), London: Voyager, →ISBN, page 555:

quotes.text: I sipped at a drink and smoked cigarettes in a silence so profound that I could hear the susurrus of the blindfold's soft fabric rustle and slip between my fingers.
quotes.reference: 2004, Gregory David Roberts, Shantaram: A Novel, →ISBN, page 613:

quotes.text: I walked steadily toward the pennant pole amid a sea of susurrus murmurings.
quotes.reference: 2007, Patrick Rothfuss, The Name of the Wind, →ISBN, page 301:

quotes.text: Bod could feel the Sleer listening to Jack's words, could feel a low susurrus of excitement building in the chamber.
quotes.reference: 2008, Neil Gaiman, The Graveyard Book, →ISBN, page 262:
